elements.text: We're not replacing small claims court. We're replacing the group chat argument that never actually ends.

Questions

What people ask before filing.
Can anyone read a public case?

Yes. Public cases are designed to be opened and shared by anyone. You only need to sign in when you want to vote or file a case.

Can anyone read a public case?
Yes. Public cases are designed to be opened and shared by anyone. You only need to sign in when you want to vote or file a case.

How is the verdict decided?

The verdict is based on the stored for and against vote totals. There is no hidden consensus score.
The verdict is based on the stored for and against vote totals. There is no hidden consensus score.

Do I need a password?

No. Internet Court uses Google sign in, so you can enter without creating or remembering another password.
No. Internet Court uses Google sign in, so you can enter without creating or remembering another password.

Can I report a case?

Yes. Every public case has a reporting path for abuse such as harassment, threats, personal data, hate and spam.
Yes. Every public case has a reporting path for abuse such as harassment, threats, personal data, hate and spam.

Is filing a case free?

Public cases are free to file. Membership is for people who want more control over their cases and identity.

Does Internet Court use fake votes?

No. The product is built around real authenticated votes and server side checks. Nothing is seeded.

        - generic [ref=f3e102] [box=24,1891,720,621]:
          - generic [ref=f3e103] [box=24,1891,720,95]:
            - heading "Can anyone read a public case?" [level=3] [ref=f3e104] [box=24,1891,720,21]
            - paragraph [ref=f3e105] [box=24,1918,720,47]: Yes. Public cases are designed to be opened and shared by anyone. You only need to sign in when you want to vote or file a case.
          - generic [ref=f3e106] [box=24,2006,720,71]:
            - heading "How is the verdict decided?" [level=3] [ref=f3e107] [box=24,2006,720,21]
            - paragraph [ref=f3e108] [box=24,2033,720,23]: The verdict is based on the stored for and against vote totals. There is no hidden consensus score.
          - generic [ref=f3e109] [box=24,2097,720,95]:
            - heading "Do I need a password?" [level=3] [ref=f3e110] [box=24,2097,720,21]
            - paragraph [ref=f3e111] [box=24,2124,720,47]: No. Internet Court uses Google sign in, so you can enter without creating or remembering another password.
          - generic [ref=f3e112] [box=24,2212,720,95]:
            - heading "Can I report a case?" [level=3] [ref=f3e113] [box=24,2212,720,21]
            - paragraph [ref=f3e114] [box=24,2239,720,47]: Yes. Every public case has a reporting path for abuse such as harassment, threats, personal data, hate and spam.
          - generic [ref=f3e115] [box=24,2326,720,95]:
            - heading "Is filing a case free?" [level=3] [ref=f3e116] [box=24,2326,720,21]
            - paragraph [ref=f3e117] [box=24,2353,720,47]: Public cases are free to file. Membership is for people who want more control over their cases and identity.
          - generic [ref=f3e118] [box=24,2441,720,71]:
            - heading "Does Internet Court use fake votes?" [level=3] [ref=f3e119] [box=24,2441,720,21]
            - paragraph [ref=f3e120] [box=24,2468,720,23]: No. The product is built around real authenticated votes and server side checks. Nothing is seeded.
